([[Powder Springs, Georgia]]) | college = [[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn]] (2019–2020) | highlights = * Second-team All-[[Southeastern Conference|SEC]] (2020) * SEC All-Freshman Team (2020) * SEC All-Defensive Team (2020) * [[Nike Hoop Summit]] (2019) | medal_templates = {{MedalSport|Men's basketball}} {{MedalCountry|{{bk|USA}}}} {{MedalCompetition|[[FIBA Under-17 Basketball World Cup|FIBA Under-17 World Cup]]}} {{MedalGold|[[2018 FIBA Under-17 Basketball World Cup|2018 Argentina]]|[[United States men's national under-17 basketball team|Team]]}} }} '''Isaac Okoro''' (born January 26, 2001) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn Tigers]]. Listed at {{convert|6|ft|6|in|m|2}} and {{convert|225|lbs|kg|0}}, he plays the [[small forward]] position. Okoro played basketball for [[McEachern High School]] in [[Georgia (U.S. state)|Georgia]] for four years, helping his team win the state championship and achieve national success in his senior season. He was considered a five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] by [[Rivals.com|Rivals]] and a four-star recruit by [[247Sports.com|247Sports]] and [[ESPN]]. After his freshman college season at [[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn]], he was named to the second team All-SEC. ==Early life== Okoro was born in [[Atlanta|Atlanta, Georgia]] to Nigerian parents and was raised close to [[Atlanta metropolitan area|metro Atlanta]]. His father, Godwin, emigrated from [[Nigeria]] in the 1980s. His mother, Gloria, also originates from Nigeria.{{cite web |last1=Givony |first1=Jonathan|title=Isaac Okoro: 2019 Hoop Summit Interview |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jo4xHsN9bTk |website=[[YouTube]] |accessdate=April 11, 2019 |date=April 11, 2019}} Okoro started playing basketball in his local church league. When he was around seven to eight years old, he began training under the guidance of [[Amateur Athletic Union]] (AAU) coach Omar Cooper, the father of his future high school teammate, [[Sharife Cooper]]. He played for the A.O.T. Running Rebels of the Nike EYBL circuit.{{cite web |last1=Scarborough |first1=Alex |title=Auburn back to the Final Four? Only if Isaac Okoro gets selfish |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/28679298/auburn-back-final-four-only-isaac-okoro-gets-selfish |website=[[ESPN]] |accessdate=February 21, 2020 |date=February 12, 2020}} ==High school career== Okoro played high school basketball for [[McEachern High School]] in [[Powder Springs, Georgia]]. In his freshman season, he averaged 15 points and eight rebounds per game, helping his team win the regional title and reach the [[Georgia High School Association]] Class 7A state quarterfinals.{{cite Montgomery Advertiser|language=en-US}} ===Recruiting=== By the end of his high school career, Okoro was considered a five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] by [[Rivals.com|Rivals]] and a four-star recruit by [[247Sports.com|247Sports]] and [[ESPN]].{{cite web |title=Isaac Okoro |url=https://auburntigers.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/isaac-okoro/14897 |publisher=Auburn University Athletics |accessdate=April 29, 2020}}{{cite web |title=Auburn freshman Isaac Okoro to declare eligibility for NBA draft committed to play [[college basketball]] for [[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn]] over offers from [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida]], [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State]], [[Oregon Ducks men's basketball|Oregon]] and [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas]], among others.{{cite web |last1=Vitale |first1=Josh |title=Isaac Okoro, ranked 35th nationally in 2019 edge Vanderbilt 83–79 to stay perfect |url=https://collegebasketball.nbcsports.com/2020/01/08/okoro-no-5-auburn-edge-vanderbilt-83-79-to-stay-perfect/ |accessdate=January 9, 2020 |work=[[NBC Sports]] |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=February 15, 2020}} After the regular season, he was named to the All-SEC Second Team, the SEC All-Freshman Team and the SEC All-Defensive Team by the league's coaches.{{Cite web|url=https://www.secsports.com/article/28877731/sec-announces-2020-men-basketball-awards|title=SEC announces 2020 Men's Basketball Awards|publisher=[[Southeastern Conference]] |date=March 10, 2020 |access-date=March 10, 2020}} Okoro averaged 12.9 points, 4.4 rebounds and two assists per game. After his freshman season, he announced that he would enter the [[2020 NBA draft]].{{cite news |last1=Boone |first1=Kyle |title=Auburn freshman Isaac Okoro, projected lottery pick, set to test NBA Draft waters |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/auburn-freshman-isaac-okoro-projected-lottery-pick-set-to-test-nba-draft-waters/ |accessdate=March 20, 2020 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=March 20, 2020}} ==National team career== Okoro played for the [[United States men's national under-17 basketball team|United States]] at the [[2018 FIBA Under-17 Basketball World Cup]] in Argentina. In seven games, he averaged 4.3 points, 1.9 rebounds and 1.6 steals per game, helping his team win the gold medal.{{cite web |title=Isaac Okoro (USA)'s profile - FIBA U17 Basketball World Cup |url=http://www.fiba.basketball/world/u17/2018/player/Isaac-Okoro |publisher=[[FIBA]] |accessdate=July 27, 2019}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}} ===College=== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"| [[2019–20 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2019–20]]{{cite web |title=Isaac Okoro College Stats |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/isaac-okoro-1.html |publisher=[[Sports Reference]] |accessdate=April 29, 2020}} | style="text-align:left;"| [[2019–20 Auburn Tigers men's basketball team|Auburn]] | 28 || 28 || 31.5 || .514 || .290 || .672 || 4.4 || 2.0 || .9 || .9 || 12.9 {{S-end}} ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== *[https://auburntigers.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/isaac-okoro/14897 Auburn Tigers bio] *[https://www.usab.com/basketball/players/mens/o/okoro-isaac.aspx USA Basketball bio] {{DEFAULTSORT:Okoro, Isaac}} [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:2001 births]] [[Category:African-American basketball players]] [[Category:American men's basketball players]] [[Category:American people of Nigerian descent]] [[Category:Auburn Tigers men's basketball players]] [[Category:Basketball players from Georgia (U.S. state)]] [[Category:Small forwards]] [[Category:Sportspeople from Atlanta]]
